records.title: Physiological Mishap Experience: 1 January to 31 March 1984
records.locator: Printed pp. 24–26, Figures 1–4 and Flying Smart — Reporting Smart?
records.note: Primary USAF first-quarter Class C physiological surveillance. Figures report 4 bends mishaps and 4 affected people. The diagnosed F-15 episode belongs to those four. No flight-level risk set or link to the wider USAF safety archive is available. Full text recovered through Firecrawl from the official issue. The original PDF byte digest is unavailable.

milestones.note: Planned right-engine shutdown during a functional check flight.
The cabin indication was 30000 ft. The reported delay is between engine shutdown and noticing the indication. Duration above 25000 ft remains unknown.
Pilot descended to FL200 and remained there until normal cabin pressure was restored. Exact pressure and timing are unknown.
The one-hour total covers the entire functional check flight.
The same evening, several hours after the flight, leg tingling and left elbow pain began. The precise delay is unknown.
Symptoms persisted into the next day. The flight surgeon diagnosed bends. An exact contact time is unavailable.
The report documents hyperbaric treatment and no reported recurrence. The treatment table and observation time are unavailable.
This is the grounding duration. Individual clinical assessment times are unavailable.

records.title: C/KC-135: 1985 mishap review
records.locator: C/KC-135, pp. 11–15, Figure 1 and Class C and HAP Mishaps
records.note: Primary 1985 fleet report. Two separate bends mishaps are among five pressurization mishaps with physiological problems and 12 total reportable Class C/HAP pressurization mishaps. Affected headcount and all-flight exposure denominator are unknown. Full text recovered through Firecrawl from the official issue. The original PDF byte digest is unavailable.
